Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you clean up this request into a prompt for a short dye-log entry for the navy cotton batch D-214 in vat 3. the operator is checking the bath during the 20 minute hold, and the acceptable temperature is 60 to 62 C for the whole hold. we need the log entry to say what happens next, not make up test results or claim anything already happened. if the bath remains in range for all 20 minutes, tell the writer to record that the standard rinse may begin after the hold. If it goes outside that range at any point, the entry should instead say to keep the batch on hold, not begin rinsing, and record the actual temperature and time of the out-of-range reading. don't blend the branches or treat a brief excursion as acceptable. include batch and vat identification and a place to enter start and end times for the hold. Keep it brief and usable by a shift operator, with straightforward wording. no need for dye chemistry or an explanation of why temperature matters, and don't decide which branch applies because readings have not been provided. The hold is planned as a 20 minute step, but no temperatures, date, or operator name are available. Make the conditional directions easy to scan.", "output": "Write a brief, clear dye-log entry prompt for the navy cotton batch D-214 in vat 3. The operator will check the bath during the planned 20-minute hold. The acceptable temperature range is 60 to 62 C throughout the entire hold.

Include the batch and vat identification, plus spaces to enter the hold’s start and end times. Make the next step conditional:
- If the bath remains within range for all 20 minutes, direct the writer to record that the standard rinse may begin after the hold.
- If the bath goes outside that range at any point, direct the writer to keep the batch on hold, not begin rinsing, and record the actual temperature and time of the out-of-range reading. Do not treat a brief excursion as acceptable.

Keep the directions easy to scan and usable by a shift operator. Do not invent test results or state that anything has already happened. No temperature readings, date, or operator name have been provided, so do not decide which branch applies. Do not include dye chemistry or an explanation of why temperature matters."}]
